interpretive_note: A Barcelona / Catalonia commercial gazetteer in mercantesca cursive. The upper block gives exchange ragguagli for cloth/yarn goods (Milanese, Como, Brescia, Florentine) converting "in Barcelona" or "in the said place" in robe/rotoli and once. A short travel-and-lodging block follows (Tarascona, Belghama, Avignon) with entry-and-lodging charges in soldi/denari. The lower block lists spices and trade goods sold at Barcelona — wax, dates, saffron(?), camlet, galls, etc. — each with a quantity (up to N t°), a quality term, a tare (pesa av. 2), and the customs duty / selling charge (sporto / dssesa a usanza). A foot brace ties four Romagna/Catalan place names to a note on very bad wools sold by balance-weight.

A wool gazetteer of (largely Catalan/Aragonese) towns; for each: quantity put out in libbre (lb), quality, how it weighs out, and the export charge "to Pisa" in soldi (s.) and denari (d.) per *sommo*.

- **Algora**: gives lb 400 *sommonali* (medium) wool of Catalonia, [reputable?/honest]; weighs out, charge to Pisa, wool s. 2, d. 2¼ per sommo; lb 5¼ per sommo.
- **Visello**: gives lb 800 good; weighs, export s. 2¼ per sommo, fine, to Pisa.
- **Agermiriza / Cappola / Fredis / Clospigiera** (braced): from lb 600 and 700, *sommonali* wools; weigh out at the same charge up to Pisa; export s. 5, d. 6 per sommo.
- **Goronimo / Penarogia** (braced): lb 650, bad wools; weigh at the charge, export up to Pisa s. 7, d. 8 per sommo; lb 5¼ per sommo.
- **Orcella**: lb 1000 bad *sommonali*; some bad, some not [improvable?]; charge up to Pisa s. 4 per sommo; weigh per sommo.
- **…gholo**: lb 200 *sommonali*; export to Pisa s. 5 per sommo.
- **Itoro**: lb 400 good; weigh, charge s. 5 per sommo, fine, up to Pisa.

interpretive_note: A wool gazetteer (ragguaglio delle lane): a systematic list of mostly Catalan/Aragonese supplying towns, recording for each the quantity given out in libbre, a quality grade (buone/sommonali/chattive), how it weighs out, and the export charge "a Pisa" in soldi/denari per sommo. Groups of towns are braced to share a single note, and closing entries cross-reference one another ("as much as Villa fremosa"). It served as a merchant's procurement/pricing reference for the Catalan wool trade routed through Pisa.

**English translation (approximate).** Spanish/Aragonese wools by district with bale-weights, quality, the grade "terunolo" (= Teruel wool), and freight-and-charge to Valencia. lb = pounds; f = florins; d = denari.

- *Sferro / al Ghastellanio*: lb 300, quite good, it is Teruel wool; shipped to Valencia at f 2.
- *Ghado*: lb 300, good, of "strech"; first inland then to Valencia; carried to Valencia at f 2¼.
- *Diamante* lb 400 / *Argiento* lb 700 / *Volava* lb 250 / *Paviali* lb 600 / *Poghalisos* lb 250 / *Agniodalida* lb 700 — all good wool and Teruel grade; first to Teruel then Valencia, charge f 2.
- Of *Ghabrea* and the whole Ghabra district, about lb 1500 — bad (cattive) wool; from the district to Valencia, f 2¼.
- *Osso* dritto lb 250, good, from the district, charge to Valencia f 2.
- *Alfa* lb 400 / *Valava Ghomede* lb 400 / *Santa Valava* lb 300 / *Torra Londerera* lb 390 / *Vollofranqa* (Villafranca?) lb 390 / *Buongiera* lb 100, common; wool ... f lb ¼; *Nora* and district, charge to Valencia f 2¼.
- Wool of the Fera of the Barozzi: all good, better than the wool of the Terunna; from Teruel than the greater Torra: each per [...] d 26 for extra charge.
- *Cera / Vacca* and all their districts ... bought at the Boragizo, good and better than that of the Boragizo / ... and Ferranza // and Alaona ... of Vendrele ... and of bad quality, especially of the Morosa of the Boto.
- *Borrha Osme* ... gathered/coloured, good, and the "rova" lb 35⅔; but bought at Valencia this time.
- *Ola* good, fine wool with much short (corte) hair, rare; of *Ghalorra* and *Ellorera* lb 38½; bought at Valencia.
- Of *Ghoraggo* the Teruel wools have much hair, not very good.

**+ Duties (Diritti):**
- At Teruel, in all one pays a toll (pedaggio) for everything, lb 2.
- At the Fera of the Barozzino, of weight 40 ... per "affono" coarse.
- In all at Aragon, one pays a "commerciale" duty of 14 ... per d.
- At El Latio of Tortosa one pays the "ammaggaramza" and "dasigona" duty d 16 per somo (load).

**+ In the castle and district of Amolina:**
- *Olina / Novega / Erea / Lugaroni / Purghera / Ghovelin / Todasl* — all in the territory of Amolina and its castle; all good wool.

**+ In the mountains of Campo d'Aronza:**
- *Ife / Moinole / Mocoba / Ottoi / Piu Plenas / Mourghadella / Chulara of the Nabaros / Sferrore / Algunglo* — all in the mountains of Campo d'Aronza; all good wool, better than Campo dell'Ofqis, and the district of Ghuos.
- *Ghonsa* good / *Fimercola / Vallorret / Corsaffrora / Novaret / Consala / Gorggolio / Mainara* — of Campo d'Aronza, good and abundant wool.
- *Orcal / Ghorggno / Odne / Puyral / Blaqueo Bello / Ogni Sneragio* — in the territory of Morcale and Ghahogat; good wool.

> **+ Granata (Granada) with Barcelona — fol. 16**

- One hundred *cane* of Granada of the *carradori* converts at Barcelona to between 157 and 155 *cane*.
- And likewise, of *palmi* 10 per *cana*, and the *cana* of Granada makes 9 *palmi*.
- And 100 *donne* of Granada are at Barcelona 175 *donne*, and the *cana* of Granada at Barcelona = 1 7/20 *cana*.
- And 100 *libbre* of Granada convert at Barcelona to ... 3 and 11 ... 19 ½ and ½ d.; of Granada they are at Barcelona 1 lb.
- The "archassa" (skein/hank) of spun gold, being 60 [parts] gold, converts at Barcelona to 54 *once*.
- Per *libbra* of ... of Granada it converts at Barcelona to 10 2/4 *once* of *monete* 9, in *moneta* of balance; and of Granada 9 *once*, with a charge of 2 per ...
- The merchandise of Genoa here at Barcelona [weighs] 1 ½ *barre*, of which of 56 and one *tocco* converts at Barcelona to 63 lb, and the *libro* with charge in itself ... in the name of Barcelona, from 20 first, by proportion.
- Nine and a third *once* of Granada make one *moueḡo* at Barcelona.
- The *quintale* of wool at Barcelona, reckoned per first 190 *libbre* net and ..., the merchandise of balance reckoned for Granada, the charge reckoned for Granada, brokerage and provision of Granada, conducted in itself without insurance, 6 ⅓ per first.
- *Quadrelime* (?) ... charge reckoned for Granada in the said manner, 10 per first.
- And spun gold at charge reckoned for Granada in itself, opening of ship first and ... and the unloading; and at Barcelona one returns the *quintali grossi* ... for *cane*; ... of one, and one Barcelonese "archassa".
- Sfax (*Ffaculo*) goes via Montpellier ... at the charge for Granada and the expense of return, from 6 ⅓ of ½ per first of Granada.
- Per the ... of *marcholi* (?) in itself a half: from 62 and 62 per first per first of Granada.

> **+ Palermo with Barcelona**

- The *onza* of *garbino* [is] 30 *tarì*, the *tarì* worth 2 *carlini*, the *carlino* [is] 10 *grani*; the *durbato* worth 12 *garbini* and one *aspro* besides.
- The *cantaro* of Palermo is 1 ½ *cantara* of Barcelona, and the *padno* (cloth?) of Barcelona [is] one *cana*; 12 *cadrara rosata* (?), 1 lb per *pesa*.
- The *quintali* at Palermo [is] 100 lb, and *quintali* 1 ⅗ of Barcelona equal one *coverga* of 12 lb of Barcelona.

> **+ Charges as they are laid out**

- For "foresi" (gate/measuring duty), measuring: of *forspoy* 4 *grani*, and the *lattadno* 3 *grani* per *pezza*.
- For brokerage (*sensaria*): of *forspoy* 10 *grani*, of the *lattadno* 9 *grani*.
- For "foresi" to remove (?) *arbasa* (rough cloth) 9 *grani* per *balla*.
- For the duty (*diritto*) of the *cantaro* and per first of *forspoy* and other duties not ..., according to how each falls ... of such and [other] duties.

**+ Majorca [Manolicha] by itself**

- At Majorca there come from Barbary silks / roe(?) — from Burgundy, from Soule, from Bayonne(?), from Saluzzo(?), from Tabensi(?); they are of "Hungarian"(?) crimson(?) royal rose [quality], f. 33 per pound.
- From Treviso, from Languedoc(?) — these are not so good — "carla" rose, f. 22 per pound.
- From Alghada(?), Aone, Montfrança(?), Tunis(?) — these silks are all coarse silks; they carry duty(?) of f. 31 per pound.
- At Majorca there come very large quantities of hides from Barbary.
- Hides of Tunis, from Soule, are good "of Orsona"(?); ordinarily, weighing about 24–25 the cwt., Barbary [weight], they carry f. 79–78 per cwt., by fifths.
- Hides of Algherda(?) are of a weight of about 27 (or 19) per cwt.; hides by fifths, Barbary, worth f. 79–76 by fifths.
- Hides of Bona [Annaba], of Algiers(?), of Bougie, from 23 to 24 [per cwt.], Barbary, f. 70–72 [per cwt.].
- Hides of Aone, of Annes(?), of Mostança(?), from 21 to 19, f. 66–68 per cwt. Barbary.
- The "essembri"(?) hides at Majorca, from Brindisi(?), by the quintal Barbary are about lb. 117; and at Majorca by Romana weight, by fifths, Barbary.
- And there are plenty of Barbary lands, and the "Hungarian"(?) hides are "of Orsona stella"; and from [...], and from Aone [...] in Barbary [...].
- Others(?) come from Majorca, from Alghuda(?), Aone, worth f. 33–37 per cwt.
- And it is true noting that all the Barbary stock(?) hides, when they are "of Insevamsi"(?) and of colour with the mark(?), are many and whitish.
- The "aghouttiera"(?) at Majorca, of weight, is reckoned "of that of Barcelona".
- The "ssghassp" of weight, of Tortosa, converts at Majorca to cantar(?) 7 ¼.
- And the "inque sessory" of Marseille(?) are, at Majorca, cantar 7 ¼.
- A "salma" general(?) of Danha(?), being 16 [...], converts at Majorca to cantar 3 ¾.
- And the "dno"(?) "of the sun"(?) of [Drcunya], converts at Majorca to cantar 10 ¼; and weight by fifths(?) [...] 33–39 [...] in the meantime.

**+ Wool of Minorca [minorgha]**

- Minorca wool is weighed every [...] lb. 1 and 4 · lb. 104 at Minorca; tare lb. 4 per [...]; [...] at Marseille(?) by the same weight [...] it seals(?) at Minorca.
- Ciutadella ["Cittadella"] of the field, of Abonssensa(?), reckoned at 200 quintals, are the best of the island.
- "Chterore" and "Cterremini"(?), per 200, are good as [...]; they weigh "argello"(?) [...]; "fiomtradllo"(?) are vendable; "chormgi"(?) are good [...].
- "Daone" and "Cterremini", per 200, are good as the "golle"(?) of the other land; vendable [...].
- And the Minorcan(?), per 200 quintals, coarse, these are good of the island.
- "Borsstss"(?), per 100 quintals · the "chmondasi" and "grandasi"; these are the best, of the same kind [...].
- "Borionasi"(?) the cantar(?) of the said wools converts at Florence to lb. one hundred (100), net.

**+ Damascus, at Barcelona**
- The *gintare* (kintar/cantaro) of Damascus is 100 *ruotoli* (rolls), at 12 once to the *colonna*, and 50 [...]; at the [...] it converts at Barcelona — the charges, not maintained, about 5 p(er cent) — and it converts to 17 lb 12 [...].
- The [...] charge is 1/6; the *ruotolo* makes at Barcelona 9 once [...]; [reckoned at] 24 carats and 70 sacks make a weight [...] 6½ make once, [reckoned] the 9th of March at Barcelona.
- The first charge — not carats — ¼ or ½ or ¾, and similar charges, as understood, count toward [it].
- [So many] units, ½, of March at Barcelona make one charge of Damascus.
- The *pinzo* makes 2 3/5 *palmi* at Barcelona.
- The appraisal/spread of Damascus is reckoned at 2½[?] at Barcelona.
- The *ruotolo* is of 5 once p(er cent), and the tare makes 4½ lb; and the *garra* (gross) at 5 p(er cent) makes 4½ lb. Every consignment of Damascus [goods] is tared 5 p(er cent), and the net is paper and twine.
- And take heed: small parcels do not pay the duty levied on Damascus goods, [on] entry and exit.
- The *gintar* (kintar) [of Barcelona] is greater by 1/5 than that of Damascus.

**+ Entry-gabella (customs duty) of Damascus, and other charges**
- One pays at Damascus on goods, on entry, 7¼ p(er cent), and the seal/purse of the *moro* (Moor's office?) and of Cyprus[?] 5 d(enari) per bale; and the duty of the inspector and of the weigher 7/4 per bale; brokerage 2 p(er cent), without counting the costs of the men employed; thus on loading, from 8 p(er cent).
- One reckons the p(er cent) on entry at Damascus per bale of 10 [...] in addition, of 1.
- One brings a [quantity] of Catalan [cloth] at the cost of [duties] at Damascus itself; sold, [it does] not... amounting in proportion to [...] at 20 p(er cent), etc.
- The customs office charges per bale 1¼ per cloth, and the cloths pass at the customs office of duties at 2 per bale; and protection (escort) of duties at Damascus from 24 to 30 *charach* (carats?).
- The brokerage from the merchant to the buyer is [so much] per bale.

**+ Charges on the export (uscita) of Damascus goods**
- The duty of the *charegone* to be given per gr(osso) 1, per weighing-fee of 1¼ p(er cent) per [...] of 4 p(er cent); for the duty of the official of the *cattatore* (collector) dom — ½; and for the place-charge of Damascus 2 p(er cent); for the duty of the *colatore* (weigher) ¼ per [...]; for the duty of *rompera* (purchase?) place pays 3 [...] amounting [...] 8 for protection of Damascus customs from 70 [...] and the cloths pass at the customs of duties at 2; for the [...] and the costs the men make [for] the *raccomandatori* (consignees) 2½ p(er cent).
- The merchant pays the *disita* (deposit/tax) of Damascus to the man, of the soldi at 2 per head [bale], the ¼ net; and the customs at Damascus pays the brokerage of 12, at Barcelona, with the [...] aforesaid.
interpretive_note: A three-part mercantile memorandum on trade between Damascus (Damasco) and Barcelona (Barzalona). The first block gives the local weights and measures of Damascus — the gintare/kintar of 100 ruotoli, the pinzo equal to 2 3/5 palmi at Barcelona, tare at 5 per cent, and weight conversions (e.g. to 17 lb 12) — noting the kintar is larger than the standard by 1/5. The second block (Gabella d'intrata) lists Damascus entry customs (c. 7¼ per cent plus seal-fees, inspector/weigher duties, brokerage, handling). The third (Spese all'uscita) itemises export charges: weighing-fee, collectors' and weighers' duties, porterage/escort, brokerage, and the merchant's per-bale payments. A practical reckoning for a Florentine handling Levantine goods through the western Mediterranean.

translation_md:
- *(Heading)* The thing[s] after which they convert: in Florence and in Pisa they have, by the same weight... the gross/large [weight] and that of the commune of Florence.
- The *cantaro* of Genoa is [gross?]; every *rubbio* weighs 25 lb, and of *garbo* weight 150 lb should convert in Florence to 138 lb.
- The Sardinian *cantaro* is 8 *rubbi* of Genoa, which would make 200 lb of *garbo* weight, and converts in Florence to 180, [or] 184 lb.
- The *cantaro* of Naples is 25 *rubbi* of Genoa, which is 275 lb of *garbo* weight, and converts in Florence and Pisa to 250 lb.
- The *cantaro* of [Nîmes / "l'uomo"?] is 30 *rubbi* of Genoa; it converts in Florence to 110, [or] 125 lb. And 102 *libbre* of Lucca convert in Florence to 100 lb.
- [Grain]: from there it converts, accurately assayed, [at] 35¾ *sona* of Florence.
- A *salma* of grain there converts to 25¼ *sona* at... monte; [the other measure?] does not convert well.
- A *salma* there converts from Genoa to 2½ *ayme* of grain; by Florentine measure two *ayme* of grain convert from the *garbo* measure.
- A *salma* of barley there converts to... ½... of grain.
- A [measure] of grain of Rome is 8½ to 9 *sona* of Florence; reckon it 8¾ *sona*.
- 23 *harfissi*[?] of Seville, converted in Florence and by weight, [is] *staio* 25 of the Alfonsine... they come to 4¾ for me.
- Grain at Barletta... of every... is 7½ *salme*, which converts [to] three *moggia*, at the charge of *tratta* (export duty)... ½ its *sona* for the other charges.
- The *harfisso* of grain of Catalonia [Calonga] converts at Barcelona [to] two and a half *quartini*; and the said *harfisso* of Catalonia converts [to] eight and a half *sona* by the measure of Florence.
- The *staio* of [Arles, "dorli"] is larger than that of [Aigues-Mortes, "dasgnomonta"] by ⅕, that is: every hundred *sestieri* of Arles convert at Aigues-Mortes to one hundred [and twenty?] *sestieri*.
- The *rasiere* of grain of Cagliari [cassero] of Sardinia converts [to] a *mina* of garbo, [or] by the measure of Florence 3⅛ *sona*. The *rasiere* at Bonifacio... 20 per...; two *tonchi*[?] of [grain] of Naples at Castellammare... and they are conformable to three *sona*.
- *(Textile/colour note)* ...*taffetà* of Bologna or of Florence... Catalonia, take note: ⅓ green / ⅓ green / ⅔ vermilion / of the whole piece 35, noted 35 lb; ⅔ vermilion / ⅓ vermilion / ⅔ green / 4 of *gengoly*[?]; 1 tawny and 1 black; ⅛ tawny / 1 black.
- Hides by the use of Florence should convert together [to] 104 lb.
- Hides by the use of [Domo]... can [be sold] at Ancona, by the same weight... of Florence.
- Hides by the use of Florence from [Ancona] which convert at Perugia / Siena / Gubbio / [Sgarrurero]... and by that measure 102 to 104 lb.
- Hides by the use of Bologna convert in Florence [to] 104 lb.
- Hides by the use of Seville convert in Florence [to] 190 lb, and every... Seville at the said weight... it weighs eight *once*; and this... would convert in Florence to about 7½ *once*.
- The *moggio* of salt... [from] Florence and Pisa to Barcelona is 90, [or] 80 *staia*, which is 4000 lb of salt, the *moggio* of Florence.
- The *argenuga*[?] of Genoa... lb forty[?] of Genoa converts in Florence to lb [one hundred?] thirty.

The upper block concerns where **silver / argento** is *bandito* (officially priced / cried) and the assayer's (*argentaro*) terms: it is cried at **Palermo** and **Messina**, and likewise at **Avignon**; notes on the assay names at Palermo, Pisa and Avignon. One should bring / show cloths "of the second grade" to **Avignon** of **Florence**(?): recognition marks and a fine "quarter" of cloths — 6 pieces, black and dark purple, 1 dark green, 1 "famous"(?) and 1 *alepri* (Aleppo-grade?). At **Rome** each *vespro*(?) ... and at **Bologna**; *argento doppio* (refined silver) converts at Florence to lb [...] 2 per ⅌. At **Pisa** it is called *Sala di Pisa*, fl. 10–[..]; at **Palermo** priced 15–1[?] per thousand; bars should be sound and refined. For **gold** at tor. 24–26 *argentaro*, and at **Pisa** fl. 19¾–16 per thousand; **iron** at Pisa fl. 16 per thousand. One should provide a consignment(?) of gilt cloths for **Palermo** of good price — black and dark good purple, good dark vermilion, *alepri*, one dark *aymero*, 2 *ferrotti*, one "famous", one black — per *torone*. *Argento doppio* converts to French money(?)... and if assayed at **Pisa** they are fl. 15.

**"Salute di Spagna"** (heading) — price list of grades by marketplace (oncia = ounce, tor. = tornesi, lb = libbre/soldi, ⅌ = per).

*Left column:* grade "of the coarse" at price, on 2 tor. 2; Gonzaga(?) on. 2 tor. 24; *malietto* from Monte Vibo(?) on 2 lb 20; **Toulouse** on 2 lb 2; "of a vecale" on 1 lb 28; of Agrimonte on 1 lb 15; *Bie* of *aremogio* on 1 lb 28; *Bie* of a "vecale" on 2 lb 12; grade "of the orborda"(?) on 1 lb 24; grade from Monte Chiso(?) on 1 lb 24; *Bie* of *scharamoscho* on 14 [lb] 16; *Bie* of *alepri* on 1 lb 24.

*Right column:* grade of **Palermo** "mare" on. 1 tor.; grade of **Castelnuovo** on 1 lb; "of Aleppo of the coarse" on. 2 lb 12; *alepri* close-packed (*nominali*) on 4 lb 20 per...; *modolesi* (Modena?) close-packed, tor. 5 on. 20; of **London** close-packed tor. 12–18; "of a" close-packed *albente*(?) on 5–6; of *Abolonza*(?) on. 1 tor. 20 per piece; of **Barcelona** on 1 lb 26–28 per piece; "of a long" close-packed on. 2½–3 ⅌; of **Perpignan** close-packed.

Closing: At **Ragusa**, every ounce ... 6 and tor. 30 = one ounce; every 20 grains = one *tornese*; each *tornese* is worth d. [...] in *carlini*(?). One *cantar* of **Naples**(?) converts at **Florence** to lb 290.

Beneath, under the rubric "Salute di Spagna," a two-column table lists grades (probably saffron/dye/cloth) priced in ounces, soldi and tornesi across markets from Toulouse, Aleppo, Modena(?), London, Barcelona and Perpignan to Palermo and Castelnuovo. It closes with Ragusa weight/coin ratios and a cantar-to-libbre conversion into Florence (lb 290).

interpretive_note: A units-of-sale glossary classifying trade goods by the measure or count in which they are bought/sold. By the cantaro grosso (144 lb): bulk raw materials and chemicals (lead of Venice, iron, sulphur of Pisa/Naples/Seville, dates, soaps, flax, sinopia, cheeses of Sardinia and Castile). By the dozen: skins and leathers (sheepskins, cordovans, parchment, Parisian and Flemish skins, fish-glue). By the piece: cloths (Florentine, fustians, Spanish satins, veils, cottons) and furs (sables, martens, vair, wild cats). By the bale: linens of Champagne/Montpellier and dyed greens. By the hundred: crossbow stocks, ox-hides, Venice planks, fir lance-shafts. Further classes by the gaffio and by weight, with Florentine weight equivalences.

(Heading) *Here we shall record at Genoa (Genova) the customs, measures and weights according to the merchant Sibandino at Genoa.*

- At Genoa one records each kind of merchandise / the venture(?) for the calibration of Genoa per…
- One records [it] by ton and by ton of … [units uncertain].
- One records *soldo cberudo*(?) … the *barili* of … 7. A barrel makes one Neapolitan *botte* (cask).
- One records wine … and they are barrels; one [is a] Neapolitan [measure]; the barrels are one *mezzeruola*; they are weighed not…
- One records grain at … which are lb …; 1[…] 280 di Genova [makes a] *lamina* coarse.
- One records cloths of every region [it] is sold by the piece — save English cloths and *bronzetti* of Vol[terra?], which are recorded by ton at Genoa; this is in order; and the region of Palermo, [where] they are sold; one [unit] at Florence — money 1/16.
- At Genoa silks are recorded by *palmi*; and one gives [this] merchandise … estimated as customary; another levy at Genoa for payment of d. 8(?) per [unit] to the *almotacén* (weigher) at the *cappa* and the consuls … once at the *cappa* the consuls; and that which first is loaded inside is unloaded(?) afterwards; not many times at Genoa the country *almotacén* consuls … once.
- One [thing] is reduced(?) within another thing… *avena* … large bundles [?] of the *reila*…
- One records the *avinto* (measure) at the pound; *calegha*; lb 11 ¼ grain; the rest holds at d. 11; d. 10/12(?).
- One bale of *palmi* of Genoa converts at Barcelona [to] one *gomma* ※ 1 5/9(?).
- One *gomma*, *alaona* by *palmi*(?), converts at Barcelona [to] one *gomma* ※ 1 5/9, 10(?).
- From Genoa one exports Levant spices, likewise Lombard wares, fustians, Spanish merchandise; estimated *gomesghail*(?) and Lombard goods and all of the Ponente (West). The region of Genoa answers in the ledger as lb 7⅖ the *denaro*(?).
- From Genoa one exports the *avinto* and gold thread, *giundagi*(?), linen cloth, the leather of the *taverano*(?), thread of *chomagye*(?); and many large *ghastorme* [?], small [things] for … to the Levant.

(Heading) *To Genoa, to compare: we have lb 100 of Genoa [reduced] to Florentine.*

- Lb 100 of Genova convert: Palermo lb 106, Pisa lb 96, Bologna lb 88, Florence lb 92, Milan lb 94, Avignon lb 80, Montpellier lb 80, Barcelona lb 78, Seville lb 83, Paris lb 6?, Venice lb 72, Naples lb 94, Rome lb 90, and Caffa lb 99.
- One pound of silver of Genoa converts at Alexandria [to] *pesi*/ounces ½, *dirhem*(?).
- One pound of Genoa converts at Alexandria by weight: *dirhem* 6, lba 7/4(?).
- Spices 2¼ of cinnamon make 1 [unit] of Genoa.
- Spices three of Marseille(?) … make 1 [unit] of Genoa.
- Spices two of *dovely*(?) make 1 [unit] of Genoa.
- *Tare* twenty of *algarsmo*(?) make ounces 62 to 63 of Genoa.
- One *alma* general of *davlia*(?) is ounces 2¼ at Genoa.
- One *alma* coarse of *diluha*(?) is ounces three of Genoa.
- One *alma damigiana* is ounces 1 2/4 at Genoa.
- One *voglio* of Rome [is], at Genoa, ounces 1⅞.
- One *ogno* of Marseille cleared(?) is, at Genoa, ounces 3⅛.
- One *ogno* of Florence, which made *staia* 24, converted at Genoa [to] ounces — g ½; and *ogni staia* 4¼ to 2 make one ounce of Genoa.
- One *ogno* of *rossato*(?) is, at Genoa, ounces g ¾; and at Florence *staia* 22.
- One *hariso* (Arezzo?) of Seville is ounces g 5/4 [of] Genoa.

Heading: *"Summary of Florence — how it re-exchanges."* / *"Florence reckons / settles its exchange:"*

- **Pisa** re-exchanges by *conto* (account); likewise Pisa re-exchanges to Florence.
- **Siena, Lucca, Perugia** by *conto*; likewise from those places to Florence.
- **Rome** re-exchanges by *conto* of the Camera (papal chamber); and from Rome to Florence likewise.
- **Naples, Gaeta and all Puglia** re-exchange at 300 by *conto*, all the *once* of the *carlino*(?) being 98 to 90 according to [time]; the *carlino*(?) being worth 60 …; likewise re-exchange from those places to Florence.
- **Palermo and all [Sicily]** re-exchange by *conto*, being better or worse according to the times; likewise re-exchange from those places to Florence.
- **Milan**(?) re-exchanges by *conto*, of 32 *imperiali* … alum(?); likewise … to Florence.
- **[Avignon — Senione?]** re-exchanges by *conto* of the Camera; likewise from Avignon to Florence.
- **Montpellier** re-exchanges by *conto* in *franchi*(?); likewise re-exchanges from Montpellier to Florence.
- **Barcelona** re-exchanges by *conto* in Barcelonese money; likewise re-exchanges … Valencia(?), every *conto* being worth fl. 19 to 16 according to the times.
- And **Valencia and Barcelona** likewise re-exchange with Florence, so much per *conto*.
- **Paris**(?) re-exchanges by *conto* in *franchi*(?), being better or worse according to the times; and from Paris(?) to Florence likewise, Florence by *conto*.
- **Bruges**(?) re-exchanges by *conto* in *grossi*; likewise from Bruges to Florence so many *grossi* by *conto*.
- **London** re-exchanges by *conto*, one per [unit], in *sterlings*, worth from 36 to 40 sterlings according to the times; likewise re-exchanges from London to Florence so many sterlings by *conto*.
- And Florence, according to [the weights ~~alum~~], the pound at the alloy/standard of the *popolino*, which comes to 11 oz [and] 12 d. per pound.
- The pound of **Florence** converts: in **Genoa** to oz 12, d. 21; in **Naples** to oz 11, d. 18; in **Bologna** to oz 11, d. ½; in **Vignone/Avignon**(?) to oz 11, d. 6; and in **Alexandria** by writing(?) equals 112 *pesi* of the *mochoresi* weight.

- And from Florence are [issued] many small coins, and some money refusable(?) by account.
- "*Rottoli*"(?) wool comes plentifully from England, and *formaggio*(?), and of every sort … by … of so many *libbre*.

**+ Messina (wool).** In Messina one weighed everything fine by the *cantaro sottile*, weighing every merchandise, except that coarse goods (use) the said (coarse) *cantaro*, and always for all other matters concerning wool. Likewise every coarse good by the coarse *cantaro*, which is larger than the fine one by a tenth (e° 10). The *marco* of silver of Messina equals (the standard) at ?Boietta and in all that country; it converts in Florence to 7 oz 12 d.; it converts in Genoa to 8 oz 1 d.

**+ Calabria.** In Calabria plenty of grain and other cereals (biade), fine wool (trafine), cheeses, ?juniper in salt, and tuna. In Malta: citron (citrea), cottons. In Palermo: citrons, sugar, kermes-grain (grane), and tuna. There is throughout all Calabria: cloth of not very fine sort, fustians, ?armoy, oil and wine, and Milanese (goods), armour; spices not many.

**+ Bologna.** In Bologna ducats would be reckoned (abmoçena) as in Florence, Milan, (and) the Bolognese, and from these they make settlements (spacciamenti). For Milan it is reckoned (sirsombra) that the count at *cassa* is 32 d. in imperials per lira; and from Milan to Bologna likewise. For ?Bologna the count at *cassa* in *denari* of ?Cremona, and the reverse. For Paris the count at *cassa* in francs; and Paris to Bologna likewise. For Bruges the count is in *grossi* (di) ?Tournai per ?barla, grossi 36 d. 90, and one ?temporal grosso; and from Bruges to Bologna, grossi counted at *cassa*. Bologna ?sends to ?Arentinoro. For Rome 36 d. in Bologna convert to (the money) of ?Modena, grossi 35 d. The ?largoeba of Bologna converts in Florence to ?3½ (per) staio. The *marco* of silver in Bologna converts in Florence to 8 oz 11 d.; the said *marco* in Bologna converts in Modena to 8 oz 2 d.

**+ Milan (Melamo).** In Milan there are moneys of several values struck by past lords, each at its proper ?casanal value; with settlements of exchange and ?ramichotonche, which run at 32 d. in imperials. (One) governs with ?denenbo that Florence and Milan in Bologna are reckoned (abmoçena) — ?Lucca, Pisa, ?Perugia, ?Baghono — at 32 and 38 imperials, ?ordinary terms. For every part it is reckoned that at *cassa* per lira the count is in the money on which the settlements are founded, in (each) place; there are two reckonings.

**+ Barcelona**

- Sell at Barcelona spun gold wholesale; for each pound spent, the Genoa pound is returned — the Genoa pound = nine ounces at Barcelona.
- Bring to Barcelona unlimited lume/tin, sheepskins (boldroni), cotton-cloth (bambagina), lambskins (agnine), alum (aludi), dyes/grains, much saffron, honey, dates, coarse cloths, worked and unworked corals.
- Sell at Barcelona spices of every kind.
- Exporting unlimited goods: much spice, spun gold thread, torzonelli, lead/tin, cloths, fustians, and marino — they go to innolano (Milan?).
- One obtains cottons and linens of every kind, white re-..., taffeta of Bologna, and Cale whole of every type.
- Bring from Monolif(?) lume/tin; and they ship out hose-cloths.

**+ Catalonia**

- Catalonia weighs everything by the Barcelona standard: 11 Barcelona [pounds] = the Aragon pound.
- Sell silver "argentini" of the l'orto cintore standard: 120 lb of Catalonia returns 137 lb at Genoa.
- Sell another l'orto cintore standard: returns at Genoa 15 ounces.
- Sell the "ottavo" type at 36 (gelti); tarchaltea of zinzola at 36.
- Sell Barbary silver argentini at 144; returns at Genoa lb 162 and 164. The l'orto cintore of Catalonia: one grossa returns at Genoa lb 400. The linens monodoni correspond to all the gealli and make at Genoa [...] ounces; at Palermo [...] and Bologna.
- Sell every kind by the gavurde standard — by these gross haverse, the Calvo lume, and the Calzime coarse standard.
- The large quintal weighs cloth, lead, fish, salt, and other goods.
- Sell gold spun wholesale; for each pound spent the Genoa pound is returned — 8 of Genoa for 10 of Catalonia in ounces.
- Sell refined silver by the cantar per the Barcelona standard; in March 8 ounces returns 7½ ounces; fine, 5½ of Catalonia make 60 ounces at Genoa.
- Bring to Catalonia: grain, lume/tin, glass, almonds, honey, lambskins, sheepskins, woad/dye in grain, cloth, hazelnuts, goods of every kind, wheat, barghino, dõmo, dates, rice, gonza, and cloths.
- A cafisso of grain at Catalonia returns at Florence 8 [staia] and a half / mr 30.
- One obtains spices of every kind, much coral, cottons, linens, fustians, garbi, iron, and marino, which go to innolano (Milan?).
- Exporting unlimited goods of every kind: cottons, gold, spun silver, and torzonelli.
- One obtains white grosana cloth, taffeta of Bologna, lead, whole salt, and cloths of Florence — the end.
- ① They are stamped/sealed properly with their money at Barcelona.

translation_md:
**Paris.** Payments in France are made in *franchi* (the gold franc): a mark is worth 12¼ in the better francs, the franc is worth 16 s. of Paris money; the francs are exchanged against the royal moneys. **Bruges** exchanges per franc reckoned in grossi — 23 grossi to the franc, 34 to 36 ... All spices are sold by the pound of 100; the *cantar/rotolo* converts to lb 169 (or lb 160); silk = 16¾ once (16¼ at Flanders); everything sold by the pound, in Paris money, 16 s., converting per florin; spun gold by the pound. *Wares drawn from France:* fine cloths, Brussels, Montivilliers, Bruges, Chartres, Provins wools, fine linens of Reims; spices of every kind — verzino colombino, cinnamon, ginger, gums, roots, sugar, etc.

**Bruges.** Several gold moneys run; exchange to every part of the world, the *muda* money of 23 grossi understood as one [Flemish] franc. The *Noble of Flanders* = 72 grossi (= 202 carlini at Paris[?]); the *Crown of Flanders* = 36½ (London money = 54); *gold lilies*/écu and crowns of Florence = 90 carlini (at London 58½ s.); *francs of Florence* = 23½ grossi (gold money 48). They bought money; carried at its own price, 40 grossi. *Exchanged at London:* 24 grossi. Every spice sold by the pound, coarse spices at so-many grossi the pound, 23 grossi understood per florin. 400 lb at Bruges = a *cantara* of [Damascus?] net lb 520; reckoned by weight at lb 650; wine/oil/salt sold by the barrel (tonello); ... 1100 per bale; [cambric?] cloth weighs 180 lb at Bruges; 100 lb at Bruges = lb 137¼ at Florence.
interpretive_note: A two-part ragguagli (exchange/weight-conversion) survey of the northern markets of Paris and Bruges: monetary equivalences of the French franc, the Flemish/Florentine noble, corona, scudi/gigli d'oro and franchi against muda/Paris/London moneys; conversions of the spice and silk cantaro to Florentine libbre and once; and lists of French export cloths (Brussels, Montivilliers, Provins wools, Reims linens) and spices/dyes. Many coin and weight figures are partly trimmed or abraded and read with reservation.

translation_md:
**✠ Damascus**

- In Damascus everything is dealt in one money, called the *dattaro* (dīnār), worth florins of gold fl. 23–24; the *dattaro* takes more or less according to the bezants in use.
- All heavy (bulk) spices are sold by a weight called the *chontaro* (qintār). The said *chontaro* converts in Venice to lb 982. The "florin" of a *tolo* (raṭl?) of the said Venice *chontaro* is lb 9, oz 10 t. By the said raṭl every fine (light) spice is sold.
- The *cottinaro* of *pingi* (ginger?), dealing in all fine goods that they sell, converts at oz 8, dl 20 in Venice.
- One sells *asarone*, figs called *ple*; seven *asaroni* are oz one good [uncertain] in Venice.
- One sells cloth that, reckoning each aretine *aro* of *pingi* at *vento* (twenty?) *pugi*, comes in Venice to a *broma* of eighty-eight.
- The *centaro* 1¼ of Damascus converts there to one good *chontaro*. Four *dattari* of Damascus are worth one bezant of *argi* (silver?).
- Exported: sturgeon[?], cottons, abundant spices, silk cloths, golden figs, pearls, and other coarse goods.
- Imported: cloths of Florence, of Lombardy, *almoghnardo*, linens, *chamo barni*(?), oil, honey, and almonds.
- We affirm *vesimatte* and sundry sorts [are] goods of Catalonia.
- [Imports continue:] *ovasse*, chestnut[-dye?], sulphur, quicksilver, copper, tin in bars, iron, *aprene* of Milan, *aviento ladeo*, salt, *mteo*, black, and corals.
- Damascus, when it sells off all its spices by weight, converts in Venice to lb 982 // in Genoa lb 950; the said *chontaro* is held [valid].
- Damascus, when it weighs 100 fine goods and 100 *degns*, converts the said florins-weights in Venice to oz 8, dl 20 // and in Genoa to oz 8, dl 8.
- Damascus, when sold by *asfsegio*(?), converts to lb 7 *sagi* in Venice, oz one good // and in Genoa to dn. 7 *sagi*, dl 22½.

**✠ Cyprus**

- In Cyprus there are two monies: white bezants and saracen bezants.
- *Char an noto* [a coin] is worth 3 t in *aldonigi* of Cyprus [uncertain].
- Exported: *dapesi*, ginger, ginger-powder, copper *de metes*, *vombollotti*, *hotoni* (cottons) spun, *borsmm*, and all spices.
- Imported: non-fine cloths of Florence, of Lombardy, *almoghnardo*, *mervne*, *amrlomo*, and some manufactured [goods].
- The hundredweight (*centenaro*) of *argi* (silver?) converts [in Genoa?] in Venice lb 750 // in Cremona lb 720 // in France lb 656 // in Rome lb 631 // in Naples lb 661 // in Bologna lb 627 // in Milan lb 668 // in Avignon lb 670 // in Montpellier lb 670 // in Barcelona lb 554 // in Seville lb 590 // and in Paris lb 948.
interpretive_note: A two-part commercial gazetteer for the Levantine markets of Damascus and Cyprus, recording each market's local money (the dattaro/dīnār valued in gold florins; Cypriot white and saracen bezants), the principal spice weights (chontaro/qintār and cottinaro) with their ragguagli into the Venetian and Genoese pound and ounce, and lists of exports versus imports. It closes with a long ragguaglio table converting the Cyprus hundredweight of silver(?) into the pound of a dozen European marketplaces from Venice to Paris.

**Heading.** This [?] shall be noted: the law (legge) made in the year 1420 concerning foreign persons who wish to dwell in Pisa; and likewise concerning the merchandise brought in and out of Pisa, [which] shall be allowed to pass; and by the first chapter (capitolo) they ratified the said law on 18 November in the aforesaid year.

**1.** If any merchandise should be brought into Pisa from the Levant (Levante) or West (Ponente) — by "Levant" understanding Rome and southward, by "West" Genoa and southward, or from any island, by sea via Calabria, for the Pisan harbor or [points] outside the Arno — and were carried out again by sea, or otherwise, within the year from its entry, sent (or were it sent) to Genoa or southward, or roundabout, or northward, no customs duty (gabella) or toll (dazio) need be paid on entry or export.

**2.** In another case, if the merchandise should change its owner, the export duty must be paid; and if within the year it were not taken out, or taken out by sea — not by the open sea[?] between Genoa and Rome — or indeed by land, … to whatever place one pays both entry and export duty, as set out above in the present concession (permissione).

**3.** Furthermore, if any merchandise [is] brought into Pisa, by sea or land, which were taken out of Pisa at any time to be conveyed into Lombardy, or which by transit had to pass through Lombardy to be conveyed into Germany (Allemagna) or any other part of the world, no customs duty need be paid on its export.

**4.** Furthermore, if any merchandise should be brought into Pisa from Lombardy, or from elsewhere via Lombardy, which were taken out of Pisa to depart within four months from its said entry into Pisa, to convey it into whatever part of the world, no customs duty or toll need be paid on entry or export.

**5.** And it is declared that if it be taken out within the said four months, one must pay [only] half (la metà) the duty for entry, and on land that of the export; and if taken out by land during the four months, but thereafter, one must pay the whole duty, both of entry and export.

**6.** And further, [as to whether] for the aforesaid goods, or some of those written above, in any part the [aforesaid] deduction is not understood, nor is effect/benefit of any kind given … and let them remain as at present they are.

**7.** Furthermore, if one should bring merchandise into Pisa which has a term in which it may be withdrawn — under some benefit one must give surety (sodare) thereupon regarding the export duty — that merchandise, or likewise on its behalf, by sufficient sureties (mallevadori) who can be no other: let them be either Florentines or Pisans present in Pisa, or to pay the due duty … should it have to, by any contingency (avvenimento) whether of time or of circumstance.
interpretive_note: A copy of a Pisan customs statute (legge) of 1420 in seven numbered chapters, regulating the gabella/dazio on merchandise entering and leaving Pisa and on foreign merchants settling there. Provisions turn on geographic origin/destination (Levante = Rome and south; Ponente = Genoa and south; islands via Calabria; transit via Lombardy to Germany or elsewhere), on change of ownership, and on time-limits (within the year; within four months with a half-duty rebate), concluding with a surety requirement that mallevadori be Florentines or Pisans resident in Pisa. Reflects the Florentine commercial regime over Pisa after 1406.

translation_md:
**13.** In our [court/land], that the ordinance which forbids that a claim cannot be made against foreigners shall not apply for that merchandise which is founded[?] … nor for goods passing in transit.

**14.** In our [land], that any foreigner who shall come … henceforth to dwell in Pisa[?] shall be exempt from every levy (gravezza) for the term of twenty years … nor [shall] he or his heirs[?] by this reason be liable to be charged, neither in person nor in goods nor in any other manner whatsoever, under penalty of [so many] lire. — Concerning this, neither passage-toll nor the ordinary customs duties (gabelle ordinarie) are understood [to be included].

**15.** In our [land], besides this, [it shall be enforced/observed] for the said term of twenty years, for every debt, obligation or contract made at any time henceforth — dated the 25th of December in the year one thousand four hundred and fourteen (1414), at folio 33 of the first [book].

**16.** And in any place and for any reason, [by] writing or public instrument[?] drawn up, by this reason he shall not be molested under the aforesaid penalty, neither in person nor in goods.

**17.** And this is not to be understood for that which might arise[?] from any Florentine, or one subject to the Comune of Florence.

**18.** And all the aforesaid things are to be understood and observed in good faith … and [this is] all confirmed[?] solemnly through the appropriate councils of the people and Comune of Florence.
interpretive_note: A copied legal/statutory text rather than a commodity table: numbered clauses (13-18) granting foreign merchants who come to dwell, apparently in Pisa, a twenty-year exemption from levies (gravezze) and protection of person and goods against claims for prior debts, obligations or contracts, dated 25 December 1414 and confirmed by the councils of the people and Comune of Florence; ordinary customs duties and passage-tolls are expressly excluded from the exemption. Reflects Florentine policy toward Pisa after the 1406 acquisition.

Wage list of galley personnel, each with a monthly salary in florins (fl.):
- the head of the salary roster (comito[?]), … per month, who is not to be passed over — **fl. 12**
- one already engaged, nine per month — **fl. 9**
- the man of counsel, who handles the galley… etc., per month — **fl. 10**
- a servant/factor, eight per month — **fl. 8**
- … who wishes to be a good servant … understanding the work — **fl. 6**
- … seven, wishes to be a manager/overseer — **fl. 7**
- the *ramolano*[?] (deck hand), eight per month — **fl. 8**
- the *maestro d'ascia* (ship's carpenter), seven per month — **fl. 7**
- the *maliscalco* (farrier/smith), seven, lacking[?], per month — **fl. 5**
- the under-*maliscalco*, four per month — **fl. 4**
- the *ghuscio*[?], who … and a half per month — **fl. 2 ½**
- the *calafato* (caulker), seven per month — **fl. 7**
- the *compagnoni* (oarsmen), experienced and good, lacking[?] about six, per month
- the *prodieri* (bow-men) and *portolani*[?], per month — **fl. 5**
- … as the said land/place …, about four per month

Prose — *"Moreover we reckoned in all, among the companions … final accounts … 60 … of oarsmen 166 of oar[?] … in this number; and as for the under-… , the watch[?], the cook[?] … likewise; in all there are 230 men besides the patron."*

*"…what is provided to the companions, by the companions, the gardeners[?]/cortolinai…"*

Victualling notes: ship's biscuit (buschotto) issued by the *scrivano* (purser) at d. 2 [denari]; fresh provisions given three times as customary, by the ounce, and salad; cheese (formaggio) by the ounce or sardines (sardelle); a daily morning ration kept fresh; wax/lac to refine, as it is worth; merchandise they handle, every Monday[?].
interpretive_note: A ricordo (memorandum) of the soldamento d'una galea — the manning and monthly wages of a galley. The list covers standard galley personnel (comito/master and deputy, uomo di consiglio, ramolano, maestro d'ascia = ship's carpenter, maliscalco and under-maliscalco, calafato = caulker, compagnoni = oarsmen, prodieri and portolani), each paid so many florins per month (fl. 12 down to fl. 2½). The prose tallies the full complement — about 166 oarsmen, "in tutto sono uomini 230 sanza l'apadrone" (230 men besides the patron) — and details the crew's victualling: ship's biscuit issued by the purser (scrivano), fresh and salted provisions, cheese, sardines, and a daily morning ration. Heavily abbreviated and abraded.
topic: Wage roster and victualling of a galley crew (soldamento d'una galea)
hardest_lines: The entire lower prose block is severely abraded; the sub-heading line ("...cortolinai/Costantinopoli?") and the victualling lines about wax/lac and the Monday ration are largely conjectural. Several personnel-role openings in the list (e.g. "sterdamo", "ghuscio", "ramolano") and the right-column entries lacking a florin figure are uncertain.

- (A line on the *gholpardarue[?]* — truly fitted at the appointed point of the hull[?].)
- When one arrives at any port, the galley is ordered to land [unload] entirely; and
- when [the men] are to take on water in the maremma(?) [on shore], [?] and the crew... one [conduit?].
- Before [it] departs, [those] of the... the helmsman(?), and let the guard and the captain(?) of the watch(?)... so that no one may approach the (?)...
- The helmsman(?), chiefly,... keep watch together with them, so that in the chief watch(?)...
- only the **compagnoni** — they are called *compagnuoli*(?), not *usinali*.
- Item, [there is] one man... the [crossbowman / balestriere?], who at night(?)... does his duty.
- When the **sail** [vela] is made [set], one is to put the bonnets(?) [bende]... [crossbowmen?].
- In the [foreship?] under the [hood/cabin] of the **gherone** [the triangular sail-piece].
- Likewise [there must be] good provisioning(?); the *usinali* are the [best-equipped/sound?].
interpretive_note: This recto is a maritime/galley memorandum (opening "Nota dichome una galea...") rather than a commodity or ragguagli table. It describes how a galley is to be ordered, crewed and equipped: its officers and crew (soprastante overseer and deputy, comito sailing-master and under-comito, a consolio council, a siniscalco steward), specialist crew (calafato caulker, maestro d'ascia carpenter, barbiere surgeon, a balestriere crossbowman) and a complement of 18 usinali making up the body of compagnoni; it also covers banners and pennons, the battle-oath (saramento da battaglia), watch-keeping and unloading in port, taking on water ashore, and rigging (vela, gherone). The prose is fast and badly abraded, so most readings are insecure.
topic: Memorandum on the manning and outfitting of a galley (officers, crew, banners, oath)
hardest_lines: Most of this prose page is abraded and the cursive is very compressed; lines reading "heredmore d(e)masshime hoxptemo heffono g(en)oh hochomo aussone alla ghuarda..." and "e i ghonpagnoni solamonte h(ann)osi giama henpagnuem gnone lefinali" and the final three lines (bela/bende, brstomam sotto chapana, adore buono ponvamento chusinali sono lebelmiti) are largely conjectural. The terms ostuvano (=soprastante?), gholpardarue, doscalea in the heading, and several officer-titles are uncertain.

interpretive_note: A provisioning and equipment checklist headed "Provedimento alla galea[?]" (provisioning for the galley), each item opened by the scribe's looping entry-initial and closed by a "need" formula (al bisogno suo, qualche bisogno, facendo al maggio[r]).
